content:
<Rep. Joseph D. Morelle>: Committee Democrats have long maintained that the Librarian of Congress should be appointed by Congress and, in that event, the United States Copyright Office (``USCO'') should retain its historic and rightful place in the legislative branch of the federal government. The amendment in the nature of a substitute agreed to by the Committee at the mark-up achieves this end by preserving the partnership enjoyed by the Library of Congress (``LOC'') and the USCO for over 150 years.
This arrangement benefits both entities and the diverse communities and users they serve. The LOC selects works deposited with the Office to include in its collections,\1\ contributing greatly to its already world-class collections. The USCO benefits from the LOC's vast operational infrastructure for information technology, physical and cyber security, workforce management, facilities, and related support services. The LOC and the USCO have been closely coordinating on technological advancements for the copyright system to make it easier to use and more accessible. Relying on LOC support services allows the USCO to devote its time and resources to the mission-specific responsibilities of the office.
\1\17 U.S.C. 704.
Even the slightest interruption in USCO's daily operations would have disastrous effects on current and prospective copyright holders as well as members of the public around the world who use USCO and LOC services. To avoid that, the USCO will continue its reliance on LOC support services to fulfill the mission of both entities.
The USCO also has a special relationship with Congress. By law, the Register of Copyrights is Congress' chief advisor\2\ on the myriad and complex copyright-related issues that impact a trillion-dollar global industry. The balance between robust protections for copyright holders and the general public's need to access knowledge and culture is best ensured when the laws passed by Congress are informed by the USCO's impartial expertise and independence. This relationship with Congress has made the legal and regulatory framework that governs American intellectual property rights the gold standard, particularly with respect to copyright.
\2\17 U.S.C. 701(b)(1).
As with the LOC, the Government Publishing Office (``GPO'') is a legislative branch agency whose agency head should be appointed by Congress. The amendment in a nature of a substitute agreed to at the mark-up also accomplishes this goal.
Committee Democrats support H.R. 6028, as amended, because it thoughtfully protects Congress's prerogatives, supports the interests of both USCO and LOC, as well as GPO, and preserves the sizeable economic and cultural obligations shared by all four.
Joseph D. Morelle,
Ranking Member.
